text:
m1 - FIX VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY on e7b6498. I filed this, so I checked it rather than assuming.

Touching WarOfTheGhostsExpectations.recallParaphrases FIRST, then WarOfTheGhostsModel.model: 10 paraphrases, 71 situations, clean. That is the exact sequence that produced four fictitious validation errors an hour ago. Probe run and deleted.

THE GUARD TEST IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I ASKED FOR, and I want to say why rather than just accept it.

I suggested "a test that touches Expectations before Model". That would have been WEAK, and I did not notice until I read theirs: suites share a JVM, so if any earlier suite had already initialised WarOfTheGhostsModel, my test would touch an Expectations that finds the Model warm and PASS WITHOUT TESTING ANYTHING. It would have been green from the day it was written and green after a regression - a test whose outcome depends on suite ordering, guarding a bug about ordering.

WarOfTheGhostsInitializationSuite loads both objects in an ISOLATED URLClassLoader, so the order under test is the only order that exists. That removes the dependence entirely.

AND IT CARRIES ITS OWN POSITIVE CONTROL, which is the part I would highlight for anyone copying the pattern: it asserts `expectations.getClass.getClassLoader eq loader` and the same for the model - "escaped isolation". Without that, a classpath the loader cannot enumerate would silently fall through to the parent, both objects would load in the normal loader, and the test would pass while isolating nothing. With it, that case fails loudly. That is exactly the tripwire-needs-a-control point I have been making all day, applied by someone else to a hazard I had not spotted in my own suggestion.

Verified: the suite passes on e7b6498.

One residual, not a defect and not worth a bead: the test is fixtures/.jvm only, correctly, since URLClassLoader is JVM-only. So the JS and Native builds have no equivalent guard. I do not think they need one - the cycle is a JVM class-initialisation phenomenon - but if the fix ever regresses in a way that manifests on another platform, nothing here will catch it. Recording it so the limit is known rather than discovered.

Recommend closure. Not closing it myself.
